questions.q: What does the code ‘hum’ stand for in the given code language?
questions.s:
“you are so gorgeous” is coded as “ntj kpr yui opj”-----------(i)

“can’t say so are” is coded as “yui bnb ntj icy”-----------------(ii)

“you anything so face” is coded as “ctr opj yui opd”----------(iii)

“gorgeous you to can’t” is coded as “hum kpr bnb opj”------(iv)

From equations (i) and (ii), we get that,

are → ntj

From equations (i), (ii) and (iii), we get that,

so → yui

From equations (i), (iii) and (iv), we get that,

you → opj

From equation (i) and (iv), we get that,

gorgeous → kpr

From equations (ii) and (iv), we get that,

can’t → bnb

From equations (ii), we get that,

 say → icy

From equation (iii), we get that,

anything/face → ctr/opd

From equations (iv), we get that,

to → hum

We get that “to” is coded as “hum”.

I. यदि पहला घटक एक सम संख्या है और अंतिम एक विषम संख्या है, तो पहले और अंतिम घटक के कोड को आपस में बदलना है।

II. यदि दूसरा और तीसरा दोनों घटक सम संख्याएँ हैं, तो इन दोनों का कोड K होगा।

III. यदि पहला घटक एक संख्या है और अंतिम एक प्रतीक है, तो पहले घटक के लिए भी अंतिम घटक के कोड का उपयोग किया जाना है।

questions_hin.q_hi: If GANGA is coded as 711471, how will YAMUNA be coded?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Letters are coded by their position in the alphabet.

G=7, A=1, N=14, G=7, A=1 → 7-1-14-7-1 → 711471 ✓ .

Apply to YAMUNA: Y=25, A=1, M=13, U=21, N=14, A=1.

Concatenate: 25-1-13-21-14-1 → 2511321141.

questions_hin.q_hi: What does the code ‘hum’ stand for in the given code language?
questions_hin.s_hi:
“you are so gorgeous” is coded as “ntj kpr yui opj”-----------(i)

“can’t say so are” is coded as “yui bnb ntj icy”-----------------(ii)

“you anything so face” is coded as “ctr opj yui opd”----------(iii)

“gorgeous you to can’t” is coded as “hum kpr bnb opj”------(iv)

From equations (i) and (ii), we get that,

are → ntj

From equations (i), (ii) and (iii), we get that,

so → yui

From equations (i), (iii) and (iv), we get that,

you → opj

From equation (i) and (iv), we get that,

gorgeous → kpr

From equations (ii) and (iv), we get that,

can’t → bnb

From equations (ii), we get that,

 say → icy

From equation (iii), we get that,

anything/face → ctr/opd

From equations (iv), we get that,

to → hum

We get that “to” is coded as “hum”.

2.(c) तर्क: वर्णमाला में अक्षरों के स्थानीय मान का योग।
